Huevia RAW development uses LibRaw 0.22.3, Copyright LibRaw LLC and other authors
listed in the accompanying COPYRIGHT file. LibRaw is used under LGPL version 2.1.
The alternative upstream CDDL license is also retained for reference.

The complete LibRaw source archive matching this build is included in this APK as
assets/third-party/libraw/LibRaw-0.22.3-source.zip.
Official original source: https://www.libraw.org/data/LibRaw-0.22.3.zip
Original SHA-256: 114ca5cf9f774114cb99ce7acbb521af5f6895e76372098ea4bef5741bd089ac
The bundled BUILD-IDENTITY.json identifies the actual source and libraries. The
standard Huevia build uses the unmodified official source. Replacement builds
made with -AllowModifiedLibRaw bundle their matching modified source instead.

libraw.so is a separate dynamically linked shared library. The JNI bridge source,
Java RAW adapter, settings model and reproducible build script are included beside
the source archive. Build with Android NDK 28.2.13676358 / API 26. Both 64-bit
ABI sets have 16KiB-compatible LOAD segments. The official NDK 32-bit libc++
runtimes retain 4KiB alignment for legacy 32-bit Android processes. Per-library
alignments are recorded in BUILD-IDENTITY.json. The application does not prohibit
reverse engineering for debugging modifications to this LGPL-covered library.
An ABI-compatible libraw.so may be substituted; when changing its ABI, rebuild the
included bridge. Repack/sign/install a modified APK using Android's normal tools.
Use a distinct runtime version string or clear the private RAW development cache
when changing decoding behaviour. Existing RAW originals must remain untouched.

LLVM libc++_shared.so is provided by Android NDK r28c and is covered by the bundled
LLVM-NOTICE.txt (Apache 2.0 with LLVM exceptions and the listed component notices).

This build enables Android system zlib, not optional RawSpeed, Adobe DNG SDK,
external JPEG/JPEG2000 or proprietary decoder plugins. Unsupported camera modes
and damaged RAW files return an error; they do not fall back to an embedded JPEG.
Full active-pixel development feeds an 8-bit sRGB PNG workspace. The Java image
editor is not a persistent linear 16-bit RAW pipeline.
